transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey Dr. Smith. Thanks for seeing me. So, what made me come in is... man, for the past year or so, the absolute smallest thing just completely pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop myself. 

Like, my phone buzzes, or somebody walks past my office. I've got this glass-front office at work—which, by the way, seemed like a killer idea when we leased the building. I dropped out of high school to start this company, so when we finally got a real headquarters, I wanted that whole "accessible CEO" vibe, you know? Total transparency. The contractors charged a fortune for the custom glass. But now it’s just people walking by all day, waving or looking in, and I completely lose my train of thought. 

Or, hell, even just a random thought about my in-laws will pop into my head and I'm totally derailed. Speaking of, they’re flying in this weekend and my father-in-law always insists on renting this massive SUV even though it's just the two of them, and it barely fits in my driveway. I keep telling him to just get a normal car, but he won't listen. He thinks he needs it for the luggage. But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just get pulled off track by every little thing lately. It's driving me crazy.
Over this past year, have you also noticed periods where your mood felt unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, along with needing much less sleep than usual but still feeling full of energy?

High or euphoric? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get my normal hours, I'm totally dragging the next day. 

Actually, speaking of sleep, my wife just made us buy one of those smart mattresses. You know, the ones that track your heart rate and actively cool down on your side? The salesman at the store was so aggressive about it. He kept showing us the app on his iPad, but honestly, I don't even like having my phone in the bedroom, let alone my bed connecting to the Wi-Fi. Our Wi-Fi at the house is terrible anyway because we live out near the hills. I had to buy three different signal extenders just to get a connection out in the garage so I could stream music while I work on my motorcycle. It's a vintage Triumph, I've been trying to restore it for... 

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, the energy and mood thing. Yeah, no, nothing like that. I sleep fine, no weird euphoric highs or anything. Just the getting pulled off track all the time.
Aside from getting distracted, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, family, or health—and have a hard time stopping that worry once it starts?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about things I can't control. Like health, for instance—my wife is always on me about eating better, but I don't worry about it because I feel fine. 

She actually just bought this massive, industrial-grade cold-press juicer to try and get me to drink more vegetables. I'm telling you, this thing weighs like forty pounds and takes up half the kitchen island. Which is incredibly annoying because we just remodeled that kitchen last year to get more counter space. We tore out these awful, ugly 90s oak cabinets. The contractor we hired was a total nightmare, though. He kept ghosting us for weeks at a time to go surfing in Costa Rica. Who runs a business like that? I mean, I run a company, and if I just disappeared to catch waves, my investors would have my head. We ended up having to fire him and finish the backsplash tile ourselves, which... man, grouting is way harder than it looks on YouTube. I completely ruined a perfectly good pair of raw denim jeans. They were imported, too. 

But, uh... sorry, what were we talking about? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really get stuck in my head worrying about stuff like that. Just the distraction thing.
Thinking back to when you were a kid, like in elementary school, did teachers or family ever mention that you had trouble paying attention or staying focused, even back then?

Yeah, actually, looking back, it was definitely happening when I was a kid, too. I mean, teachers were constantly moving my seat. I remember my fourth-grade teacher moved my desk right up next to hers. She had this massive, heavy wooden desk, kind of like the new conference table I just bought for the office. We had it custom-built out of reclaimed barn wood. It looks amazing, but getting it up to our floor was a total disaster. The freight elevator broke down, so the delivery guys had to carry this giant slab of wood up three flights of stairs. I felt so bad for them I ordered them all lunch from this new Neapolitan pizza place downtown. They have this authentic wood-fired oven imported straight from Italy, and the crust is just... man, it's incredible. My wife and I went there for our anniversary, but the wait was like two hours, which is ridiculous for pizza, you know? 

But, uh... wait. Sorry. My seat in school. Right. Yeah, they were always moving me around because I just talked way too much. Or I'd just get up and wander around the room without asking. I was always blurting things out, too, like right in the middle of a lesson before they even finished asking the question. So, yeah, I guess it's been going on for a while.

Would you say these attention and distraction issues have actually caused real problems for you—like mistakes at work, missed deadlines, or friction with your wife or colleagues—or do you manage to work around them okay?

I mean, I’m still keeping up overall. I manage. But... well, yeah, it does cause some friction. Like with my wife, we had these family plans last weekend to go up the coast. The coast is just beautiful right now, though the traffic on the 101 is an absolute nightmare. I was driving my truck, which I actually just put a new suspension on. Lifted it two inches. The shop that did it totally screwed up the alignment, though. It was pulling to the right the whole way up to Santa Barbara. Santa Barbara has this amazing seafood place right on the pier, they do this clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl that is just unreal. The seagulls there are so aggressive, though. One literally swooped down and stole a piece of bread right out of my hand while we were walking. 

But, uh... wait. Sorry, I'm doing it again. Problems. Right. 

So yeah, I'm keeping up, but it’s definitely starting to cost me some trust at home when family plans don't go the way they should because I'm distracted or bouncing around. And at work, too. I can tell people are losing patience with me. Like when I'm running meetings or having mentoring conversations with some of our newer hires, things just don't stay on track the way they're supposed to. So, yeah, I'm working around it, but I know people are definitely getting a bit fed up with me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates a lifelong (childhood-onset), pervasive pattern of inattention (easily distracted by external stimuli, tangential thought derailment, difficulty staying on topic) combined with hyperactive-impulsive features (talking excessively, blurting out answers, leaving seat without permission in childhood). Symptoms are present since elementary school, persist into adulthood, and cause functional impairment across multiple domains (work meetings/mentoring, marital/family friction). Mood episode criteria for mania/hypomania were explicitly denied (no decreased sleep need, no euphoria/irritability), and excessive worry characteristic of GAD was also denied, making bipolar disorder and generalized anxiety disorder unlikely. The clinical picture is best explained by ADHD, combined presentation (ICD-10 Hyperkinetic Disorder, F90.0).
